learningObjectives: Explain the structure and purpose of an Express.js backend.
Create REST endpoints using HTTP methods and routes.
Understand how requests, responses, and middleware work together.

activities.title: Express Architecture
activities.instruction: Click each part to explore its role in an Express application.

content.concept: An Express application organizes backend logic around an application instance, middleware, routes, request handling, and responses.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: The main Express application instance that coordinates middleware and routes.
Function that can inspect or modify requests and responses or pass control to the next handler.
Defines how a specific HTTP method and URL should be handled.
Contains information sent by the client to the server.
Carries the data and status returned by the server to the client.

activities.title: REST Method Explorer
activities.instruction: Choose the HTTP method that best matches each resource operation.

content.concept: REST APIs commonly use GET to retrieve resources, POST to create resources, PUT or PATCH to update resources, and DELETE to remove resources.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Request Response Journey
activities.instruction: Arrange the path of a request through an Express server.

content.concept: An incoming request can pass through middleware and route handlers before the server sends a response back to the client.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: REST API Builder
activities.instruction: Build a simple CRUD API for a users resource.

content.concept: A REST API exposes resources through predictable routes and HTTP methods so clients can create, retrieve, update, and delete data.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.
